socfpga_watchdog.h

Watchdog hardware abstraction driver interface for the SoCFPGA bare-metal software stack.

Types
wdt_handle_t

wdt_handle_t type is the WatchDog handle returned by calling wdt_open().  This is initialized in open and returned to the caller. The caller must pass this pointer to the rest of the APIs.

wdt_status_t

WatchDog timer status values.

Values
WDT_STOPPED

WatchDog is stopped

WDT_RUNNING

WatchDog is running

WDT_EXPIRED

WatchDog timeout timer expired

wdt_timeout_config_t

WatchDog timer timeout behavior setting.

Values
WDT_TIMEOUT_RST

Reset the device when WatchDog timeout timer expires

WDT_TIMEOUT_INTR

Generate Interrupt when WatchDog timeout timer expires

wdt_ioctl_t

Ioctl request types.

InitTimeoutTime is the initial timeout duration for the watchdog timer immediately after it is enabled. TimeoutTime specifies the duration for the watchdog timer.  The timer begins counting after the initial timeout period is triggered.  The InitTimeoutTime must be greater than or equal to the TimeoutTime. Not all platforms may support interrupt generation.

Values
WDT_SET_INIT_TIMEOUT

Set the WatchDog initial timeout value. Time shall be in milliseconds

WDT_GET_INIT_TIMEOUT

Get the WatchDog initial timeout value. Returned values are in milliseconds

WDT_SET_TIMEOUT

Set the WatchDog expire time (timeout value). Time shall be in milliseconds

WDT_GET_TIMEOUT

Get the WatchDog expire time (timeout value). Returned values are in milliseconds

WDT_GET_STATUS

Returns the WatchDog timer status of type wdt_status_t

WDT_SET_TIMEOUT_BEHAVIOUR

Set the WatchDog timeout behavior. Takes wdt_timeout_config_t type

wdt_callback_t

WatchDog notification callback type. This callback is passed to the driver by using the wdt_set_callback API. This callback is used for warning notification when the watchdog timer expires. This callback will be called only if WatchdogTimeout behavior is set to interrupt.

Parameters
param

User Context passed when setting the callback. This is not used by the driver, but just passed back to the user in the callback.

wdt_open
wdt_handle_t wdt_open(
uint32_t 
instance
)

wdt_open is used to initialize the WatchDog. This function will stop the timer if it was started and resets the timer if any was configured earlier.

Parameters
instance
uint32_t

The instance of the WatchDog to initialize.

Returns

Handle to wdt_handle_t on success.  NULL if invalid instance or instance is already open.

wdt_start
int32_t wdt_start(
const 
wdt_handle_t 
hwdt
)

wdt_start is used to start the WatchDog timer counter. WatchDog expiry (timeout) time must be set before starting the WatchDog counter. Use the WDT_SET_INIT_TIMEOUT IOCTL to set the initial timeout period and the WDT_SET_TIMEOUT IOCTL to define the regular timeout duration.

Parameters
hwdt
const wdt_handle_t

Handle to the WatchDog interface returned in wdt_open.

Returns

0 on success.  -EINVAL if hwdt is NULL.  -ENODATA if init_timeout or timeout time has not been set.

wdt_stop
int32_t wdt_stop(
const 
wdt_handle_t 
hwdt
)

wdt_stop is used to stop and reset the WatchDog timer counter.  After stopping the timer and before starting the timer again, the expire time must be set.

Parameters
hwdt
const wdt_handle_t

Handle to the WatchDog interface returned in wdt_open.

Returns

0 on success.  -EINVAL if hwdt is NULL.

wdt_restart
int32_t wdt_restart(
const 
wdt_handle_t 
hwdt
)

wdt_restart is used to restart the WatchDog timer to the originally programmed values. This function should be called periodically from a thread or the main loop to refresh the watchdog timer and prevent it from expiring. Failure to call this function within the configured timeout window may result in a system reset.

Ensure that the interval between calls is shorter than the configured watchdog timeout.  The main difference b/w wdt_start and wdt_restart APIs are, the former requires the time values are set using the IOCTLs and the latter re-uses the already programmed values and re-programs them. If restart is used without first setting the timers, it will return an error.

Parameters
hwdt
const wdt_handle_t

Handle to the WatchDog interface returned in wdt_open.

Returns

0 on success.  -EINVAL if hwdt is NULL.  -ENODATA if watchdog init_timeout or timeout time have not been set.

wdt_set_callback
void wdt_set_callback(
const 
wdt_handle_t 
hwdt,
wdt_callback_t 
callback,
void 
*
param
)

wdt_set_callback is used to set the callback to be called when init_timeout time reaches the WatchDog counter or if the timeout time is configured to generate interrupt. The caller must set the timers using IOCTL and start the timer for the callback to be called back.

A single callback is assigned per instance when interrupt behavior is configured.  Newly set callback overrides the one previously set. If input handle or if callback function is NULL, this function silently takes no action.

Parameters
hwdt
const wdt_handle_t

Handle to the WatchDog interface returned in wdt_open.

callback
wdt_callback_t

The callback function to be called.

param
void*

The user context to be passed when callback is called.

Returns

None.

wdt_ioctl
int32_t wdt_ioctl(
const 
wdt_handle_t 
hwdt,
wdt_ioctl_t 
cmd,
void *const 
buf
)

wdt_ioctl is used to configure the WatchDog timer properties like the WatchDog timeout value, WatchDog timeout behaviour etc.

Parameters
hwdt
const wdt_handle_t

Handle to the WatchDog interface returned in wdt_open.

cmd
wdt_ioctl_t

Configuration request of type wdt_ioctl_t.

buf
void* const

The configuration buffer to hold the request or response of IOCTL.

Returns

0 on success.  -EINVAL if hwdt is NULL, cmd is invalid, buf is NULL, or error in timeout behavior set.

wdt_close
int32_t wdt_close(
const 
wdt_handle_t 
hwdt
)

wdt_close is used to de-initialize the WatchDog, stops the timer if it was started and resets the timer value.

Parameters
hwdt
const wdt_handle_t

Handle to the WatchDog interface returned in wdt_open.

Returns

0 on success.  -EINVAL if hwdt is NULL, hwdt is not open (previously closed), or failed to stop wdt.
